Data audit: Every quantitative row has source/study, evidence tier, units/target definition, yield/normalization status, and censoring/missingness status.
Baselines: Canonical D0–D6 are reported on all eligible headline splits before D7+ claims.
Process signal: Process-conditioned modeling adds value over food-identity-only on a process-disjoint or equivalent controlled split; report CI/effect, not just point gain.
Kinetic fit: At least one focused D-C dataset supports an identifiable/useful kinetic fit with profile/bootstrap/posterior uncertainty.
Condition-OOD: Kinetic/hybrid/physics model adds value over the best non-kinetic tabular baseline on held-out temperature/condition.
Calibration: Real, study-disjoint calibration is reported; intervals/sets achieve acceptable task-specific coverage/width.
Abstention: Risk–coverage/selective prediction improves over always-answering and abstention rules are defined on REAL calibration data.
Consistency: Relevant non-negativity, semigroup/order/balance/constraint diagnostics are reported on scientifically valid subsets.
Completion: Evidence-aware D7 completion beats D5/D6 on masked-real-cell and cold food/process/compound/pair tests, or is rejected.

Synthetic/imputed utility: Synthetic/imputed training rows improve REAL-only study-disjoint performance in a ratio sweep without unacceptable calibration damage; no synthetic/imputed target enters final test/calibration.
Rollout: A trust horizon is empirically established on D-C/D-D where true intermediate states exist; no rollout claim otherwise.
Inverse design: At least one supported inverse-design case passes an ID-level benchmark beyond nearest-evidence/random/grid and remains inside the safe support region.
Reproducibility: Seeds, versions, hashes/snapshots, splits and parameter settings permit rerun within declared tolerance.
Human verification: Every LLM-extracted row used in held-out test/calibration is human verified against the cited source span/table.
Integration: CulinaryState-RAG / FlavorTwin end-to-end evaluation logs evidence class, uncertainty, abstention and provenance.

DATA: Are historical dates/sources usable? → sufficient dated, source-diverse corpus for stated RQ
LINEAGE: Is duplicate/edition leakage controlled? → lineage groups frozen before split
RANK: Is power-law/Zipf claim justified? → GOF + alternative comparison supports it
REPRO-K: Is Kinouchi reproduction credible? → reference summaries reproduced/documented
REPRO-I: Are Indian model baselines reproduced? → published-style baseline behavior recovered
NULL: Does pairing survive strong nulls? → effect robust to required matched controls
ID: Is recipe identity calibrated? → stable source-held-out discrimination + calibration
NOV: Is novelty more than rarity? → expert-aligned signal after rarity/source controls
QTY: Is quantity coverage adequate for soft mutation? → declared coverage/uncertainty threshold from data audit
TEMP: Does evolution beat persistence? → future-era gain beyond uncertainty
CONTACT: Does contact help? → held-out gain vs internal prevalence + shuffled-contact null
SBI: Are parameters recoverable? → synthetic recovery + coverage passes
PRETRAIN: Does simulator pretraining help real data? → real held-out gain vs real-only + random-sim control
FT: Does cultural prior improve FlavorTwin? → ranking gain without evidence-quality loss
RAG-HIST: Does historical retrieval improve evidence? → citation/UCR gain with calibrated abstention
